tools.title: MVTA - Multimedia Video Task Analysis
tools.pricing_note: Licensed via NexGen Ergonomics; ~$10k/yr University of Wisconsin consortium option
tools.inputs: Task video, annotated interactively with event breakpoints
tools.outputs: Time-study reports, event frequency, duty cycle, postural analysis
tools.description: Video task analysis software developed by Radwin and Yen at UW-Madison and distributed commercially by NexGen Ergonomics: analysts mark event breakpoints in video played at any speed or direction, and MVTA computes time studies, event frequencies, duty cycles and postural analyses. With its companion single-frame duty-cycle tool (SVDA) it supplied the duty-cycle measurements behind the frequency- and hand-speed-based ACGIH HAL equations.

tools.title: KineVid Computer-Vision HAL & Lifting Monitor

source.authors: Radwin R.G., Hu Y.H., Chen C.-H., Yen T.Y., Wang X.

tools.inputs: Conventional workplace video, markerless (no sensors on the worker)
tools.outputs: ACGIH hand activity level; lifting-task risk parameters (posture, hand/feet location, movement frequency)

patents.title: Apparatus, method and system for measuring repetitive motion activity

tools.description: UW-Madison spin-off commercializing Radwin's computer-vision exposure assessment: automatic ACGIH hand activity level from tracked hand motion in ordinary video, and a single-camera monitor that extracts lifting risk parameters aligned with the NIOSH lifting equation. Both are patent-protected (US 9,566,004 assigned to KineVid; US 11,450,148 assigned to WARF) and build on the hand speed-duty cycle HAL equation.
